newsitem.title: USA: Ethical Holdings in alliance with Searle.
newsitem.headline: Ethical Holdings in alliance with Searle.

text.p: Ethical Holdings Plc said Tuesday it had signed a strategic alliance with G.D. Searle & Co to develop and market in the United States and selected international markets a range of Ethical's transdermal patches for use in hormone replacement therapy.
G.D. Searle is the pharmaceutical unit of St. Louis, Mo.-based Monsanto Co.

Ethical, based in Stibbington, U.K., said this is its first hormone replacement therapy alliance. It will finance the development of several key hormone replacement therapy products for the United States, it said.
In exchange for licensing rights granted to Searle, Ethical has received an upfront payment of an unspecified amount and will receive additional license fee payments tied to development milestones.
Ethical retains manufacturing rights to the products and will receive a percentage of net sales on all products worldwide.
Under the alliance, Ethical will be responsible for development in the U.S. and other markets of its estrogen patch and its estrogen-progestogen combination patches.
Searle will be responsible for marketing these products in the United States, selected countries in Europe and in the Asia/Pacific region.

"This agreement is the most important step to date in the development of Ethical's U.S. strategic initiative, launched at the beginning of this year," said Ronald Albano, president of American operations for Ethical. "It provides access for a range of Ethical's (hormone replacement therapy) products to the U.S., the world's largest (hormone replacement therapy) market, and to other important markets around the world."

Richard De Schutter, Searle chairman, said the addition of Ethical's products to Searle's portfolio will help Searle extend its market reach in women's health care, a core therapeutical area for the company.
Ethical's hormone replacement therapy products are being developed to treat menopausal symptoms in women.
The alliance is subject to U.S. antitrust notification.
